subject: ventures/hard-money-loan-cost-calculator
professional: a hard money / bridge lender's loan officer or a fix-and-flip investor's CPA-analyst, who checks first that points are charged on the whole commitment, interest accrues only on drawn rehab funds, minimum-interest and extension clauses behave as on a real term sheet, and that the 'effective rate' is defined the way a borrower would compare it to an APR

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 28 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed in a separate Python script (not reading calc.mjs logic, written from the README model): (1) default deal, Lender A (85% of $200k + 100% of $60k, 11.5%, 2 pts, $1,500 flat, 3 draws at $150, hold 6, rehab 3): commitment 230,000; balance-months = 170,000*6 + 20,000*(4.5+3.5... via k/3 draws at months 1,2,3) -> interest 12,075; points 4,600; total 18,625; avg balance 210,000; simple effective rate 17.74%; tool: 18,625 / 12,075 / profit 30,975 (sale 316,200 - 200,000 - 60,000 - 6,600 holding - 18,625). Identical. (2) Lender B (90%/90%, 9.5%, 3.5 pts, 6-month minimum interest floor, 5 draws at $300): floor 234,000*0.095/12*6 = 11,115 beats accrued; total 23,305; avg balance 217,800; rate 21.40%; profit 26,295. Identical. (3) Crossover: Python sweep of months 1..14 gives A cheaper through month 10 (29,742 vs 29,946) and B cheaper from month 11 (31,946 vs 31,798); tool returns {month: 11, cheaperAfter: B}, and sensitivity rows at 3/4/6/8/10/12/15 match (within rounding at 8: 26,240 vs 26,241 from a rounding of the intermediate). (4) Simple check: $100k, 12%, 2 pts, 6 months, no rehab -> interest 6,000 + points 2,000 = 8,000, rate 16.0%; tool identical. (5) Extension: Lender A at a 12-month hold, term 9, one 3-month extension: fee 1% of 230,000 = 2,300, total 34,150; identical. Caveat checked: for case (4) a true IRR (bisection on net proceeds 98,000, six $1,000 interest payments, $100,000 repayment) is 16.19% nominal / 17.45% effective annual, versus the tool's 16.0%; the tool's 'effective annual rate' is simple cost over average balance and is not an APR/IRR, which the page does not say. Arithmetic is right for the model that is described.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page feature by running the pure functions and reading index.html: interest on drawn money only (analyze/lenderCost, tested); points on whole commitment (tested, and a mutant that drops rehab from the points base failed 4 tests); minimum-interest floor with a floorApplied flag shown in the table; per-draw fees; extension fees per block; effective annual rate; profit and return on cash; late-flip sensitivity table at 3-15 months; crossover month; CSV export (toCsv, button wired); example/reset and usage opt-out present; input warnings (negative, LTARV above 75%, hold past term). No TODOs or stubs found. Not built and honestly listed under 'Not decided' on the page and 'Not modelled' in the README: compounding/per-diem, rate bumps, prepayment beyond the minimum, closing costs on the sale (note: selling costs are modelled as a single percent). VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype. Gaps only: the CSV omits the cost lines shown in the table; rehab draws are fixed to equal spacing with no custom draw schedule.
evidence.verification: node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 28 tests, 28 pass. Seeded five mutations in calc.mjs one at a time, ran all three test files, reverted with git checkout calc.mjs (git status clean afterwards): (a) LTARV warning cutoff 75 -> 85: CAUGHT (1 fail). (b) remove the minimum-interest floor (interest = interestAccrued): CAUGHT (1 fail). (c) extensions Math.ceil -> Math.floor: CAUGHT (2 fail). (d) points base commitment -> purchaseLoan only: CAUGHT (4 fail). (e) draw timing removed (every draw counted as released at closing): CAUGHT (2 fail). 5 of 5 mutants killed, covering interest, points, floor, extensions and the warning threshold. Limits: page.test.mjs checks the HTML source, not rendered behaviour; expected values in calc.test.mjs were not seen to include a closed-form check of the effective rate beyond the author's own derivation, but my independent Python values match them.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all 154 lines), calc.test.mjs (100 lines), index.html script and head, usage.mjs by name and grep, README, llms.txt, VENTURE.yaml, robots.txt, sitemap.xml. Pure functions, no dependencies, comments explain the model, input coercion via num(), DEFAULTS as data, draws clamped to 1..1000. Defects: relative URLs in link rel=canonical (./index.html), sitemap.xml <loc>./index.html</loc> and robots.txt 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml' are not valid for crawlers; if rehabMonths > holdMonths the spread is capped silently (documented in a comment, not on the page); roi uses NaN when cash is 0 and the page formats it via pct() (would show 'NaN%' for a 100% financed deal with no points or fees, an edge case); the crossover scan only goes to 36 months and requires a sign change, so a tie region is ignored; 'cheaper' in sensitivity uses <= so ties favour A. Nothing silently wrong in the main path.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present on the page twice (the note under the header 'Not lending, legal, tax or financial advice' and a 'No warranty' footer paragraph plus the FAQ 'Is this lending, legal or financial advice?'), in the README, and in llms.txt; asserted by page.test.mjs. Checked claims: 'nothing uploaded' -> index.html imports only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs, grep for fetch( in index.html and usage.mjs found no network call; 'two-lender comparison with crossover month' -> works (above); 'interest only on drawn money' -> works; 'effective annual rate' -> computed, but defined as cost / average balance / years (simple), not APR/IRR, and the page and FAQ ('divide by the money you actually had outstanding') describe it correctly in prose but the label 'effective annual rate' will be read by many borrowers as an APR; true IRR on the control case is 17.45% effective versus 16.0% shown. FAQ example 'a 10% loan with 2 points and draw fees on a six-month flip can cost well above 15% a year' is consistent with the formula. FAQ points to 'simplifications listed under Not decided': that section exists. Defects: llms.txt links the superseded duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo address, not the live https://marisstella.app/hard-money-loan-cost-calculator/ that the README and VENTURE.yaml give; README tag line 'which used to mean comparing a headline rate against points in your head' is mild promotion. No fake reviews or usage numbers.
evidence.fitness: Walked a flipper with two term sheets: entered the defaults, got per-lender line items (interest, points, flat, draw, extension), effective rate, profit, return on cash, LTARV, a late-flip table, and the crossover month (11) in one screen without signup; that is the job. Gaps in the first hour: no per-diem or 360/365 day-count option, no custom draw schedule, no lender-specific 'points on rehab holdback only when drawn' variants, only two lenders (no third quote), selling costs are one percent figure, and CSV exports only the sensitivity rows. Warnings (LTARV, hold past term, losing deal) are the sort of guardrail a flipper wants.
evidence.domain: Compared against how hard money term sheets work (points on total commitment, interest-only on drawn funds, minimum interest/earn-out periods, draw inspection fees, extension fees as a percent of the commitment) and against how a CPA or lender quotes cost of funds. Matches those mechanics. Departures a practitioner would raise: (1) 'effective annual rate' is simple (cost / average balance / years) rather than an IRR or a Reg Z-style APR, so it understates against an IRR (16.0% vs 17.45% effective on the control case) and cannot be compared one-to-one with a lender's quoted APR; (2) interest is 30/360 monthly simple, whereas most hard money lenders charge on actual/360 per diem, which raises cost by about 1.4% of interest; (3) interest is accrued rather than paid monthly, with no cash-flow timing, so return on cash ignores the time value of the cash tied up (the page lists time value as not decided); (4) draws assumed in equal steps over the rehab period; (5) profit leaves out sale-side closing costs beyond the selling percent and taxes (listed as not decided). The method is sound for a first-pass lender comparison and honest about its limits.

defects.what: The 'effective annual rate' is simple cost over average balance, not an APR/IRR; on a 6-month, 12%, 2-point loan it shows 16.0% where the IRR is 16.19% nominal / 17.45% effective, and the page does not say it differs from a lender's quoted APR.
Interest is 30/360 monthly simple; the per-diem actual/360 convention many hard money lenders use is listed as not modelled but offers no switch.
canonical link, sitemap <loc> and robots Sitemap line use relative URLs, which search engines ignore; llms.txt links the superseded duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of marisstella.app.
roi/annualized return NaN when cash in is 0 (100% financed, no points or fees) is passed straight to pct(), which would print NaN%.
CSV export carries only the sensitivity table, not the per-lender cost lines shown on screen; page tests are regex over source and never execute the inline script.

verdict: A small, correct, honestly bounded two-lender comparison. Five independent recomputations (both default lenders' interest, points and totals, profit, the minimum-interest floor, an extension-fee case and the month-11 crossover) matched the tool to the dollar, and five seeded mutations in calc.mjs were all killed by the tests, so correctness and verification clear the bar. It scores claims 2 and domain 2 because the headline 'effective annual rate' is a simple cost-over-average-balance figure that is neither an IRR nor an APR (understating by about 1.4 points on the control loan) without a note saying so, and because the llms.txt and SEO URLs are stale or relative. Because claims is below 3 it does not meet the bar by the rubric, though it is finished (completeness 3). Cheap fixes: add a one-line 'not an APR; simple cost over average balance' note beside the rate (or add an IRR column), switch llms.txt, canonical, sitemap and robots to the absolute marisstella.app URL, guard the NaN return.
